proposal.name: Prepare Python sessions and record real test outcomes

issue_plan.name: Prepare Python sessions and record real test outcomes
issue_plan.summary: Two ordered pull requests add the directly callable Python application adapter: first validated sessions with one dependency image and complete input provenance, then isolated unittest execution with actual per-test outcomes and real Docker validation. Both update SPEC.md and README.md as behavior becomes available; public gate execution and conformance collection stay unavailable. The merger records the new session and execution policies with decision tooling and runs the required real Docker checks on the final head.

issues.title: Prepare reusable Python application execution sessions
issues.body:
Add a directly callable Python application session-preparation API in internal/verify. It validates configured invocations, stages the unchanged application and selects dependencies once, producing reusable state for the next ordered issue to execute unittest. Preparation itself executes no application code and grants no evidence. The base already has project.ResolvePythonApplication, verify.StagePythonApplication and PythonApplicationWorkspace.SelectImage; reuse these contracts rather than introducing another application-root rule or installer.

Use StagePythonApplication to preserve the full layout and exact bytes. Component references, working directories and explicit inputs are application-relative; manifest model, conformance and code paths remain verification-project-relative under #310. Keep production inventory scope unchanged. Resolve declarations from the staged snapshot and retain all original declaration fields separately from prepared execution settings. Validate every declaration before dependency selection, image acquisition or any application-execution tool; existing inert syntax discovery may still parse Python without importing it. A bad declaration anywhere must fail preparation before any install or execution, even when other declarations are valid.

Accept command exactly python with ordered arguments -m unittest followed by explicit selected test modules or individual test names; do not substitute discovery, change selection, reorder arguments or reinterpret a command string. Also validate and retain command python followed by the configured conformance driver script and literal ordered arguments. Resolve that script relative to the declared working directory, require a contained regular file and identity matching the manifest's project-relative driver and selected conformance declaration. A valid conformance declaration must not prevent preparing tests. Proof invocations, unsupported commands, interpreter/startup options, shell command strings and requests whose semantics cannot be preserved fail clearly. No declaration is ever passed through a shell. Define and document the supported unittest selection grammar and reject unsupported CLI modes rather than ignoring them.

Give each invocation its complete target/check/kind/declaration-ID identity, including duplicate IDs on different checks or targets. Detached session metadata must preserve declared command, ordered arguments, working directory, explicit environment, sampling and input hashes. Keep planned actual settings distinct: pinned absolute interpreter, trusted launcher identity (completed when execution is added), container working directory and environment must never overwrite the declaration or be presented as observed execution. The eventual executor must be able to address one exact invocation without aliasing another.

Define a finite sampling contract and defaults in the API and tests. Unit tests run their requested suite once without randomized sampling; reject nonempty test sampling rather than silently ignoring it. For the retained conformance declaration, accept runs and steps as positive integers and seed as a nonnegative integer in a documented bounded range, with omitted defaults matching current conformance values (1000, 40, 1); reject unknown keys, malformed or out-of-range values and conflicting controls. These are prepared values only: no effective conformance run is claimed. Reserve gate-owned environment/startup controls, including interpreter and import paths, hash seed, trusted launcher and output paths, sampling variables and all proxy variants; declarations cannot override them even with apparently harmless values. Reject invalid environment keys or values that cannot be passed literally. Preserve safe application values, including empty strings, whitespace, quotes and shell metacharacters, exactly.

Call the staged workspace's SelectImage and existing toolchain.PythonDepsImage once for successful session preparation. Root requirements and their recursive requirements/constraints control dependencies; verification-local requirements cannot replace them. Retain original and canonical input hashes, resolved wheel names/versions/filenames/hashes and recipe/base/platform evidence. No requirements means the standard-library path; keep SelectImage's existing return of toolchain.PythonImage with nil dependencies and no Docker call. Any acquisition needed to make that exact pinned base usable belongs in a distinct validated image-preparation step, not application execution or a changed SelectImage contract. A dependency failure, missing selected image or invalid/incomplete evidence returns no usable session and never falls back. Store the immutable selected image privately/detached from mutable caller data so later runs cannot select again or follow a replaced tag. Provide reusable state for later ordinary and larger-bound execution without implementing larger-bound conformance now.

Bind the session to every actual copied file, including unselected siblings, resources, tests, driver, manifest, ratified lock, model and local includes, plus dependency evidence. Keep generated artifacts outside that input snapshot. Provide freshness verification that rejects changed, added, deleted, symlinked or replaced staged inputs before reuse; check freshness around image preparation too. Changes to exposed inventories or caller-owned declaration maps/slices must not retarget the session or its recorded identity. Portable session provenance and its fingerprint must be deterministic across repeats and relocation, excluding host paths, temporary IDs and local image IDs/tags while preserving meaningful argument order. Original bytes remain unchanged on success, failure and cancellation; define ownership and cleanup of session resources and incomplete preparation.

Add acceptance and regression tests for all validation and no-tool-before-validation boundaries, both supported unittest selection forms, root and non-root working directories, driver resolution/mismatch, valid mixed test/conformance preparation, literal safe environment and arguments, reserved controls and sampling errors, complete invocation identity, dependency selection once, immutable state, bad dependency evidence and no fallback, standard-library preparation, whole-snapshot freshness and relocation-stable provenance. Use orchestration doubles where appropriate without claiming they execute Python. Add a reusable fixture of an ordinary task-lifecycle package importing a sibling and reading a resource, with standard-library and recursive root requirements/constraints variants (for example an actual packaging wheel pinned by a constraint); give it selected lexical tests and a driver declaration. The next issue extends this same fixture for real runtime tests and a later bound-observation issue can add an application entry point calling the selected lifecycle component. Preserve and run existing rejection, discovery and staging tests.

Keep verify.Check, verify.Run, the CLI and Python.Check disconnected from the adapter: explicit components retain ErrComponents and existing Python without components retains ErrPythonApplication before execution tools or installation. Preserve model-only checking, inert component discovery, caller-supplied component attribution, legacy Python, marked-file checks and TypeScript. This work needs no source annotations or # +nagini marker and must never invoke Nagini. Factory drafting, synthesis, proof adapters, public gate integration and conformance observation collection are outside this issue. Do not edit decisions/, pinned statements or ratified locks.

Update SPEC.md and README.md in this change to document the callable preparation API, invocation and snapshot contract, sampling defaults, dependency reuse and cleanup, while accurately saying no application executor has landed yet. Cite the recorded foundations below on changed SPEC bullets and link #313's ratified child plan; do not rewrite #310's context contract. Merger work: use decision tooling to record the new preparation/session policy and its dependencies; any unavailable Docker/network checks also belong to Merger work and alone do not require repair. The next ordered issue completes this parent's execution and real Docker requirements.

Foundations: D-0013 (tool-output evidence), D-0029 and D-0047 (conformance foundations, without enabling conformance here), D-0054 (unchanged existing applications), D-0158 and D-0168 (component and invocation declarations), D-0171 (actual runtime outcomes without inferred coverage), D-0177 (inert Python identities), D-0178 (dependency images and controlled startup), D-0180 (#310 application context) and D-0122 (current documentation). This implements part of #315, the first ordered issue of #314 in #294's Python adoption work. The extension is authorized by #313's ratified child plan: https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/313#issuecomment-6536681769, sha256:0380e0c90425c12cb24fed241112820b07758fecb6d812130b71424a857d2366; #314's ratified split is https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/314#issuecomment-6536732025, sha256:32f595456a146a9ac6b05b5b10c6a69f054fd99d5afaf02fe3f236983f3901a9.

issues.title: Execute Python application tests and retain observed outcomes
issues.body:
Build on the preceding merged session-preparation API in internal/verify to add directly callable execution of its validated unittest invocations. Complete #315's session/test adapter: run real application tests and return observed per-test outcomes with execution provenance. The preceding issue supplies staging, declaration validation, snapshot identity and one immutable dependency image. Reuse that session without installing or resolving dependencies again, including repeated uses and the state needed for later ordinary/larger-bound runs. Conformance declarations stay valid retained configuration, but any attempt to execute one must return an explicit unsupported result with no conformance evidence; bound observations remain the next issue of #314.

Execute the exact prepared target/check/kind/declaration-ID invocation. Preserve command meaning, ordered module or individual-name selections, argument values, application-relative working directory and literal safe environment. Use an argument vector and a new trusted unittest launcher; do not repurpose runConformance's legacy shell script or interpret declaration strings as shell. Record the unchanged declaration separately from what actually ran: pinned absolute interpreter and flags, trusted launcher path and content hash, actual ordered arguments, container working directory, explicit effective environment and effective sampling. Use the preceding issue's single unsampled suite execution for tests, rejecting conflicting or unsupported controls. Repeated declaration IDs on different checks/targets must never merge outcomes.

Use existing toolchain.Docker isolation and cancellation cleanup. Every execution uses the session's exact immutable selected image with no pull, tag lookup, reinstall, fallback or re-resolution. Failure when the selected image disappears must be explicit. Image acquisition is a preparation operation, separate from application execution; installation network remains confined to the existing dependency-image builder. Run offline with proxy suppression, memory and process limits, no host environment or credentials, and separate trusted runtime, application inputs and generated output. Source runs from the staged layout with the declared working directory. Prevent input modification where possible, check the whole snapshot before and after each run and between session uses, and invalidate successful evidence when bytes, membership or input identity changed. An execution-time mutation may not acquire success under old hashes. Preserve the original application byte-for-byte on success, failure and cancellation, and clean up containers and temporary outputs.

Preserve #227/D-0178 startup semantics in the new launcher: use the pinned /usr/local/bin/python, disable site/user-site processing and implicit source paths, keep PYTHONHASHSEED=0 actually effective (do not use -I in a way that ignores it), and establish trusted standard-library and runtime paths before application imports. Application root and configured driver directory precede installed libraries. Protect both regular application packages and nested namespace packages competing with dependency regular packages; path order alone is insufficient. Installed scripts, .pth, sitecustomize and usercustomize must not take over startup. Application or dependency names cannot shadow trusted runner/standard-library code during startup. Imports of admitted dependencies are application execution, not trusted tooling.

Collect observations from the actual unittest runner, using a structured, validated output protocol separate from arbitrary application stdout/stderr. Identify which configured lexical test declarations really ran, for both module and individual-name selections; selected names alone are insufficient. Bind observations to actual staged source identities, so an overwritten or substituted same-named method cannot credit a different lexical declaration. Preserve runtime order and diagnostics. Keep success, failure, error, skip and nonexecution distinct. Account for loader/import errors, fixture/setup errors, subtest failures, expected failures/unexpected successes and unsuccessful or interrupted process completion without turning them into successful required tests. Retain outcomes already observed even if a later test, loader or process fails. Missing, unexecuted, skipped or failed required tests cannot qualify for later success even when another test passes or the process exits zero.

Reject empty, malformed, missing, truncated, contradictory or identity-mismatched runner output as incomplete/invalid evidence; never infer completeness from exit zero. Retain valid observations already obtained with an explicit incomplete/unsuccessful overall result when final output is missing. Validate that protocol records belong to this session, invocation, runner and input snapshot, and that reported tests actually match configured lexical declarations; arbitrary printed success records must not stand in for runner observations. Keep process completion, per-test results and evidence completeness separately visible. Return raw execution outcomes and provenance; do not infer production target coverage, fabricate assertion records or grant proof, model conformance or project assurance. Leave caller-supplied attribution APIs intact.

Bind every result to all staged file hashes from the session, dependency recipe/base/platform and original/canonical hashes and wheel evidence, plus trusted launcher/runner content identity and actual execution settings. Include unselected siblings/resources, tests, driver, manifest, ratified lock, model and local includes without expanding production scope. Portable serialization and fingerprints must be deterministic for identical repeated or relocated runs, exclude host paths and temporary container/run IDs and execution-only image IDs/tags, and retain meaningful argument and observation ordering. Keep operational diagnostics available without allowing host-specific temporary paths or incidental execution metadata to make otherwise equal portable evidence differ.

Add acceptance and regression tests against real Python execution as well as orchestration doubles. Cover both unittest invocation forms, literal ordered arguments/environment, non-root working directories, declared-versus-actual metadata, duplicate IDs on different checks, all test outcomes/nonexecution, loader errors and partial completion, malformed/missing/mismatched protocol output, snapshot changes including unselected inputs and changes during a run, repeat reuse with one image selection, image disappearance with no fallback, conformance unsupported without blocking tests, unchanged originals and cancellation cleanup. Retain the previous issue's validation-before-tools tests and ensure all public rejections and legacy/model-only behavior remain unchanged. Doubles may test invocation orchestration and fault injection but cannot replace real Python in outcome or startup validation.

Add real Docker tests under the prefix TestPythonApplicationExecution. Extend the preceding issue's unchanged task-lifecycle fixture: it imports a sibling, reads a resource and uses an installed third-party wheel from recursive root requirements/constraints; run a standard-library variant too. Keep the fixture suitable for the next bound-observation issue to add an application entry point calling the selected lifecycle component. Run through the production session/executor, not a test-only substitute. Exercise actual module and individual selections, pass/fail/error/skip/missing tests and partial execution, non-root working directories, repeated and relocated deterministic evidence, dependency reuse and complete wheel evidence. Test actual hash-seed behavior, trusted startup, regular and nested namespace precedence against hostile dependency packages, suppressed .pth/site/user-site hooks and installed-script takeover, offline networking and uppercase/lowercase proxy suppression, cancellation with no surviving container, and unchanged original bytes after success and failure. Include controls that establish hostile startup/import fixtures would take over without the production isolation. When INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_EXECUTION_REAL=1 is set, the real suite must run and fail on missing prerequisites or execution failure rather than silently skip.

Keep verify.Check, verify.Run, the CLI and Python.Check disconnected from the adapter: explicit components retain ErrComponents and existing Python without components retains ErrPythonApplication before execution tools or installation. Preserve model-only checking, inert component discovery, caller-supplied component attribution, legacy Python, marked-file checks and TypeScript. This work needs no source annotations or # +nagini marker and must never invoke Nagini. Factory drafting, synthesis, proof adapters, public gate integration and conformance observation collection are outside this issue. Do not edit decisions/, pinned statements or ratified locks.

Update SPEC.md and README.md in the same change to describe the now-available direct session/test executor, its supported invocation and evidence contract, sampling and image reuse, and its limitations. Remove blanket claims that no direct application adapter exists while retaining accurate statements that public existing-Python gate execution and conformance observation collection remain unavailable. Changed SPEC bullets cite the recorded foundations below as appropriate and link #313's ratified child plan. Do not change #310's application-context contract.

Merger work: record the new execution-session/runtime-test policy and its dependencies using decision tooling, then run INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_EXECUTION_REAL=1 go test ./internal/verify -run '^TestPythonApplicationExecution' -count=1 -timeout 30m on the final PR head and post passing output. Decision recording and checks requiring unavailable Docker/network belong under Merger work in review and alone do not require a repair. This issue completes all execution, provenance and real validation work requested by #315; no part of #315 is deferred to the later conformance-observation issue.

Foundations: D-0013 (tool-output evidence), D-0029 and D-0047 (conformance foundations, without enabling conformance here), D-0054 (unchanged existing applications), D-0158 and D-0168 (component and invocation declarations), D-0171 (actual runtime outcomes without inferred coverage), D-0177 (inert Python identities), D-0178 (dependency images and controlled startup), D-0180 (#310 application context) and D-0122 (current documentation). This implements part of #315, the first ordered issue of #314 in #294's Python adoption work. The extension is authorized by #313's ratified child plan: https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/313#issuecomment-6536681769, sha256:0380e0c90425c12cb24fed241112820b07758fecb6d812130b71424a857d2366; #314's ratified split is https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/314#issuecomment-6536732025, sha256:32f595456a146a9ac6b05b5b10c6a69f054fd99d5afaf02fe3f236983f3901a9.
